scenes.tts: Give a guinea pig radioactive leucine, then look at its pancreas. Within about five minutes, the newly made digestive enzymes sit over the rough endoplasmic reticulum. By about twenty minutes, the label lies over the Golgi. By an hour, it is in the granules the cell will later release. How do we know that order, and how fast does the protein move?

scenes.tts: The method is called pulse-chase. First comes a short pulse of radioactive amino acid. Then comes the chase, a flood of unlabelled amino acid. Now only protein made during the pulse carries label. That labelled group is a cohort, and you follow it as it moves.
scenes.visual: Yellow dots made in the ER during the pulse, grey dots made in the chase; the yellow cohort is bracketed and travels on alone.
scenes.narration: The method is called pulse-chase. First comes a short pulse of radioactive amino acid. Then comes the chase, a flood of unlabelled amino acid. Now only protein made during the pulse carries label. That labelled group is a cohort, and you follow it as it moves.

scenes.tts: In the E R lumen, a core of fourteen sugars is attached to the protein. It passes the E R G I C and enters the Golgi at the sis face. Golgi enzymes then rebuild the sugar chain as the protein crosses to the trans side. Early enzymes act first, and galactose and sialic acid are added later. So the chain carries a stamp of how far the protein has come.

scenes.tts: Endoglycosidase H, or Endo H, reads that stamp. It cuts high-mannose chains. It does not cut the complex chains made after the early Golgi enzymes have acted. Cut protein runs faster on a gel. So the resistant band counts protein that has reached those enzymes.
scenes.visual: Endo H as scissors cuts the orange chain but not the green one; the cut protein band drops down a lane while the resistant band stays.

scenes.tts: Here is an illustrative time course. At each chase time, the two bands add up to one thousand. So the resistant share is zero, thirty-three, fifty-five, and eighty percent. The rate constant, k, comes out near zero point zero two six seven per minute at fifteen, thirty, and sixty minutes. The three agree, so one first-order step fits.

scenes.tts: Half-time is zero point six nine three divided by k, or twenty-six minutes. That covers E R exit plus the trip to the Golgi enzymes. So it is an upper bound for E R exit alone. Resistance is a threshold in a sequence, not a switch between two organelles. Keep the rule: the sugar chain records how far the protein has come.
